akhfash:2-3.t: He said ﴿وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ﴾ ﴿وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ﴾: this wāw is a wāw of conjunction, by which (the oath) is conjoined to the wāw of the first oath. And some read ﴿وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ﴾, making the oath by the creation, as if He swore by what He created, then explained it and made it a badal (substitute) for ﴿ما﴾. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the variant is printed in the same form as the standard text. The reading meant is presumably «والذكرِ والأنثى», in the genitive.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى﴾ with its darkness everything between the heaven and the earth,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى﴾: is uncovered and appears. «إذا» in both places is purely adverbial (li-mujarrad al-ẓarfiyya), and the governing word (ʿāmil) in it is the verb of the oath.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَمَا﴾ — in the sense of «من» ("who"), or maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) — ﴿خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى﴾: Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ, or every male and every female. The ambiguous hermaphrodite (al-khunthā al-mushkil) is, in our view, male or female in the sight of Allah the Exalted; so whoever swears that he will not speak to a male or a female breaks his oath by speaking to him.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ﴾: your work ﴿لَشَتَّى﴾: diverse; one works for the Garden through obedience and one works for the Fire through disobedience.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى﴾, that is, in "There is no god but Allah," in both places,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَخِلَ﴾ with Allah's due ﴿وَاسْتَغْنَى﴾ of His reward

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ﴾: We will make him ready ﴿لِلْعُسْرَى﴾: for the Fire.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَمَا﴾ is negating (nāfiya). ﴿يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى﴾ into the Fire.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَى﴾: to make clear the way of guidance from the way of misguidance, so that Our command to follow the first and Our prohibition of committing the second are obeyed.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولَى﴾, that is, this world; so whoever seeks them from other than Us has erred.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ﴾: I have warned you, O people of Mecca, ﴿نَارًا تَلَظَّى﴾ — with one of the two tāʾs of the original dropped, and it has been read with it retained — that is, blazes.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿لَا يَصْلَاهَا﴾: enters it ﴿إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى﴾, in the sense of «الشقي» ("the wretched one"),

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿الَّذِي كَذَّبَ﴾ the Prophet ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ from faith. This restriction (ḥaṣr) is to be interpreted [non-literally] because of His words, Exalted is He, {وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ}; so what is meant is eternal burning.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا﴾: will be kept far from it ﴿الْأَتْقَى﴾, in the sense of «التقي» ("the God-fearing one"),

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿الَّذِي يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّى﴾: seeking purification by it with Allah the Exalted, in that he gives it out for Allah the Exalted, not for show or reputation, so that he is pure in the sight of Allah. This was revealed concerning al-Ṣiddīq [Abū Bakr], may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, when he bought Bilāl, who was being tortured for his faith, and freed him; the disbelievers said, "He only did that because of a favour that [Bilāl] had done him," so there was revealed:

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: but he did that ﴿ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَى﴾, that is, seeking Allah's reward,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَى﴾ with the reward he will be given in the Garden. The verse includes whoever does the like of what he, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, did; he will be kept far from the Fire and rewarded.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَغْشى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:2-2.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is similar.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَما﴾: a relative noun conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الذَّكَرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَالْأُنْثى﴾: conjoined to الذكر; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ﴾: inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿لَشَتَّى﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of consequence (tafrīʿ) and resumption; ﴿أما﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَعْطى﴾: a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿وَاتَّقى﴾: conjoined to أعطى; and the clause أعطى is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the answer to من, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لِلْيُسْرى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) من.

daas-irab:8-8.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:9-9.t: Also conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is like the preceding one.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿وَما﴾: negative; ﴿يُغْنِي﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿عَنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مالُهُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿تَرَدَّى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿لَلْهُدى﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿الهدى﴾ is the postponed noun of inna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:13-13.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is like it.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object; ﴿ناراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَلَظَّى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of نارا.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿لا يَصْلاها﴾: لا is negative, and an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿الْأَشْقَى﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of نارا.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of الأشقى; ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾: conjoined to كذب.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the sīn is for the future, and a passive imperfect verb; ها is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْأَتْقَى﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of الأتقى; ﴿يُؤْتِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿مالَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿يَتَزَكَّى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿لِأَحَدٍ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿نِعْمَةٍ﴾: genitive in form, nominative in position, the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تُجْزى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of نعمة.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿ابْتِغاءَ﴾: the excepted, accusative (manṣūb); ﴿وَجْهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾: also muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْأَعْلى﴾: naʿt (adjective) of وجه.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, and the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; ﴿سوف﴾: a particle of deferral and future; ﴿يَرْضى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

farraa:17-17.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَتْقَى﴾ — Abū Bakr.

farraa:19-19.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا لأَحَدٍ عِندَهُ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ﴾.
He says: he did not spend what he spent as a recompense for a favour (lit. a hand) that anyone had done him; rather he spent it seeking the Face of his Lord. So «إلاّ» in this place has the meaning of (لكن) "but". It is also permissible to make the act of recompense refer to the future, so that you say: and he did not seek, by what he spent, a recompense from anyone. Then the place of the lām that is in «أحدٍ» would belong to the hāʾ [141/b] which «عنده» put in the genitive, as though you said: and he has, from anyone, in what he spent, no favour whose reward he seeks. Both ways are good. Al-Farrāʾ said: I do not know which of the two ways is better. The Arabs sometimes put a word in other than its place when the meaning is known. The poet said:
لقد خفت حتى ما تزيدُ مخافتى * على وعلٍ فى ذى المكاره عاقِل
(I have feared until my fear does not exceed [that of] a mountain goat taking refuge on the rugged heights.)
and the meaning is: until the fear of a (وعل) "mountain goat" does not exceed my fear. Similar to it, outside the genitive, is the saying of the rajaz poet:
إن سراجا لكريم مفخره * تحلى به العين إذا ما تجهره
(Surely Surāj is noble in his glory; the eye takes delight in him when it beholds him.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: [one says] حلِيت بعينى (I became pleasing in his eye) and حلَوت فى صدرى (I became sweet in his breast); and the meaning is: تحلى بالعين إذا ما تجهره (he is pleasing to the eye when it beholds him). [Translator's note: i.e. the verse makes the eye the subject of «تحلى», though the sense is that Surāj is pleasing to the eye — the word has been put out of its place.]
The accusative (naṣb) of «الابتغاء» [Translator's note: in the next verse, ﴿إِلاَّ ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾] comes from two aspects. One is that you take it to carry the intended sense: his spending — he spends nothing except seeking the Face of his Lord. The other is on account of the difference between what comes before إلاّ and what comes after it. The Arabs say: ما فى الدار أحد إِلاَّ أكلباً وأحمرةً (There is no one in the house except some dogs and donkeys) — this is a dialect of the people of the Hijaz. [Others] make the end of the speech follow its beginning, putting it in the nominative (rafʿ) when [the first] is nominative. The poet said concerning that:
وبلدةٍ ليس بها أنيس * إِلاّ اليعافير وإِلاّ العيس
(And many a land in which there is no companion except the fawn-coloured gazelles and the whitish camels.)
So he used the nominative. And if someone were to put (إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه) in the nominative, it would not be a mistake, because if you dropped «من» from «من نعمة» you would say: ما لأحد عنده نعمةٌ تجزى إِلا ابتغاءُ, so the nominative would be by following the meaning, just as you say: ما أتانى من أحد إِلاَّ أبوك (No one came to me except your father).

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is "والذكرِ والأنثى". If one put "الذكر والأنثى" in the genitive in our reading, he would make "وما خلق" as though He said: and by what He created of the male and the female. The general public read it in the accusative, meaning: and His creating the male and the female.

farraa:4-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ﴾.
This is the response (jawāb) to the oath. His saying "لشتى": He says: diverse. It was revealed concerning Abū Bakr ibn Abī Quḥāfa, may Allah have mercy on him, and concerning Abū Sufyān. That is because Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, bought nine men who were in the hands of the idolaters with his own wealth, seeking thereby Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, sent down concerning him: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ﴾ ﴿بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾ — Abū Bakr — ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ﴾: for returning to righteous deeds.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ﴾.
He says: he was created as one wretched, barred from good. Someone may say: How did He say: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ﴾ — is there any easing (تيسير) in hardship? It is said in reply that its permissibility is on the same footing as the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾; good tidings (البشارة) are originally for what gladdens and pleases; but when two statements are combined — "this is good" and "this is evil" — easing is permissible for both together.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ﴾: We will prepare him. The Arabs say: قد يسّرت الغنم (the sheep have become ready) when they give birth or are ready to give birth. The poet said:
هما سيدانا يزعمان وإنما * يسوداننا أن يسَّرت غنماها
(They claim to be our two lords, but they only lord it over us because their sheep have borne young.)

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying [141/a], Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ﴾.
He says: whoever follows guidance, his way is upon Allah. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَعَلَى اللهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ﴾; He says: whoever seeks Allah is on the straight way. It is also said: upon Us is guidance and leading astray, and leading astray was left out, as He said: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرّ﴾, while they protect from heat and cold.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
For the reward of this one and the reward of that one.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَاراً تَلَظَّىٰ﴾.
Its meaning is: تتلظّى (it blazes), so it is in the position of the nominative. If it had the sense of a past verb, it would be: فأنذرتكم ناراً تلظّت.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to me from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr missed a rakʿa of the sunset prayer, so he stood up to make it up, and I heard him reading: ﴿فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَاراً تَلَظَّىٰ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the point of the report suggests he read «تتلظّى» with two tāʾs]. Al-Farrāʾ said: I saw it in the codex of ʿAbdullāh: "تتلظّى", with two tāʾs.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَصْلاَهَآ إِلاَّ ٱلأَشْقَى﴾.
Except whoever was wretched in the knowledge of Allah.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
He did not deny by open rejection, but he fell short of the obedience he was commanded, so it was counted as denial (تكذيب), as you say: لقي فلان العدوَّ فكذب (So-and-so met the enemy and "lied"), when he shrank back and retreated. Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard Abū Tharwān say: "Banū Numayr have no flinching (مكذوبة) in their earnestness", meaning: when they meet [the enemy] they fight in earnest and do not retreat. Likewise the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كاذِبَةٌ﴾; He says: it is true.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied أقسم (I swear).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «ما» applies to individual rational beings, and it is a relative noun conjoined to «النهار».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (إن سعيكم لشتى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The fāʾ is a conjunction; «أما»: a particle of condition and detailing; «من»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ}, and the fāʾ is the linking one; the clause is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى}.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (فسنيسره لليسرى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is the linking one.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause; «من»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فسنيسره» is the khabar (predicate) of the relative «من».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «وما يغني» is conjoined to the clause «سنيسره»; «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied apodosis; its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being: "his wealth will not avail him".

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (إن علينا للهدى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is for emphasis.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «فأنذرتكم» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَى}; «نارا»: second object; and the clause «تلظى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «نارا».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «لا يصلاها» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {نَارًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (الذي كذب وتولى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of {الأَشْقَى}.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «وسيجنبها» is conjoined to the clause {لا يَصْلاهَا}.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «يتزكى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يؤتي».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «وما لأحد عنده من نعمة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يَتَزَكَّى}; the preposition «لأحد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «نعمة», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); «عنده»: an adverb of place attached to a ḥāl from «نعمة»; and the clause «تجزى» is a naʿt (adjective) of نعمة.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «ابتغاء» is mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «ولسوف يرضى» is the answer to an implied oath (jawāb qasam muqaddar), and the implied oath clause is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, the Exalted: (وما خلق الذكر): (ما) with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and the creation of the male and the female". It is also said that (ما) means (من) "who": Allah, exalted be His mention, swore by Himself. It is also said that (ما) means (الذي). Al-Farrāʾ allowed (الذكر) and (الأنثى) in the genitive as a badal (substitute) from (ما), taking it to mean (الذي).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (فأما من أعطى): (من) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (فسنيسره) is the khabar (predicate); it is a condition and its answer. Its like is (وأما من بخل).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying (وما يغني عنه ماله): (ما) is in the position of the accusative governed by (يغني); it is an interrogative governed by what follows it. (ما) may also be a negating particle with the object of (يغني) omitted, i.e. "His wealth will not avail him anything when he perishes."

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying (إن علينا للهدى): (للهدى) is the noun of (إن) and (علينا) is the khabar (predicate). Its like is (وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى). The lām of emphasis enters upon the mubtadaʾ (subject); upon the noun of (إن) when it is placed after; upon the khabar of (إن), unless it is a past verb or an adverbial phrase immediately following (إن); and upon an adverbial phrase when it occurs in the position of the khabar, even if it is not the khabar and the khabar comes after it. For example: (لزيد قائم), (إن في الدار لزيدا), (إن زيدا لقائم), (ليقوم), (لفي الدار), (لأبوه منطلق), and (إن زيدا لفي الدار قائم) and (لقائم). If you put (لقائم) before (في الدار), the lām does not enter the adverbial phrase, because you have brought the lām in the khabar. When the khabar is placed after, the lām may enter both, because the adverbial phrase is inoperative (mulghā).

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying (إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه): (ابتغاء) is accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Al-Farrāʾ allowed the nominative in (ابتغاء) as a badal (substitute) from the position of (نعمة), but that is far-fetched.
His saying (إن سعيكم): it is the answer to the oath. [Translator's note: this refers to verse 4, though it appears in this entry.]

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والليل﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «الليل» is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: "I swear" (أقسم).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, attached to the verb of oath.
﴿يغشى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو); the clause ﴿يغشى﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿والنهار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «النهار» is conjoined to ﴿الليل﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb of oath.
﴿تجلى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو); the clause ﴿تجلى﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun conjoined to ﴿الليل﴾, genitive (majrūr). Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and it together with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to ﴿الليل﴾, genitive.
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿خلق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿الذكر﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿والأنثى﴾: conjoined to ﴿الذكر﴾, genitive. [Translator's note: so in the source («مجرور»); conjoined to the accusative ﴿الذكر﴾ it would be accusative.]

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle.
﴿سعيكم﴾: the noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb), and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿لشتى﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «شتى» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma; the clause of «إن» with its noun and its khabar is the answer of the oath.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فأما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أعطى﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿أعطى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿واتقى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and «اتقى» is a past verb, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿اتقى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أعطى﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وصدق﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and «صدق» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿وصدق﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أعطى﴾.
﴿بالحسنى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صدق﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فسنيسره﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sīn is for deferment (taswīf), and «نيسره» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma, with a latent (mustatir) agent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿لليسرى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نيسره﴾; the clause ﴿سنيسره﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿من﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿بخل﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿بَخِلَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿واستغنى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and «استغنى» is a past verb, and the agent is latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿استغنى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿بخل﴾, and the clause ﴿من بخل﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من أعطى﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وكذب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and «كذب» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿كذب﴾ is conjoined to ﴿بخل﴾.
﴿بالحسنى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذب﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿فسنيسره﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sīn is for deferment (taswīf), and «نيسره» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the overt ḍamma, with a latent (mustatir) agent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿للعسرى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نيسره﴾; the clause ﴿سنيسره﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿من﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «ما» is negating. Or: the wāw is resumptive and ﴿ما﴾ is interrogative, for disapproval, in the position of accusative standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of ﴿يغني﴾, the implied sense being: "and what availing will his wealth avail him?" (وأيَّ إغناءٍ يغنى عنه ماله); or in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يغني﴾, the implied sense being: "and what thing will his wealth avail him?" (وأيَّ شيء يغني عنه ماله).
﴿يغني﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ.
﴿عنه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغني﴾.
﴿ماله﴾: fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, attached to ﴿يغني﴾.
﴿تردى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the implied fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿تردى﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle.
﴿علينا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿للهدى﴾: the lām is for emphasis, and «الهدى» is the postponed noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa; the clause ﴿إن علينا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وإن﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «إن» is an abrogating particle.
﴿لنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿للآخرة﴾: the lām is for emphasis, and «الآخرة» is the postponed noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿والأولى﴾: conjoined to ﴿الآخرة﴾, accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فأنذرتكم﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to something implied, and «أنذرتكم» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿نارًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿تلظى﴾: a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; ﴿تلظى﴾ here is an imperfect verb (originally تتلظى)], and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هي); the clause ﴿تلظى﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نارًا﴾, accusative (manṣūb), and the clause ﴿أنذرتكم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿إن علينا للهدى﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يصلاها﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and ﴿ها﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿الأشقى﴾: fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يصلى﴾, nominative by an implied ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الأشقى﴾.
﴿كذب﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿كذب﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause).
﴿وتولى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; a past verb indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the agent is latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿تولى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿كذب﴾, falling within the scope of the ṣila.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿وسيجنبها﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, the sīn is a particle of the future brought for emphasis, and «يجنبها» is an imperfect verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), nominative (marfūʿ), with a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿الأتقى﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الأتقى﴾, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿يؤتي﴾: an imperfect verb, and its agent is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿يؤتي﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿ماله﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿يتزكى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and its agent is latent; the clause ﴿يتزكى﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ﴿يؤتي﴾, with no grammatical position, or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of ﴿يؤتي﴾, i.e. ﴿متزكيًا به عند الله﴾ ("purifying himself thereby before Allah").

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, or resumptive, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is negating.
﴿لأحد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿عنده﴾: an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿من﴾: a connective (ṣila) preposition.
﴿نعمة﴾: a noun genitive (majrūr) by «من» in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿تجزى﴾: an imperfect verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هي); the clause ﴿وما عنده...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position, or circumstantial in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception meaning "but" (لكن).
﴿ابتغاء﴾: a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ), or mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
﴿وجه﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
﴿ربه﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الأعلى﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رب﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿ولسوف﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, the lām is the answer of a concealed oath, i.e. "By Allah, he will surely be pleased" (والله لسوف يرضى), and «سوف» is a particle of the future.
﴿يرضى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and its fāʿil (agent) is: "he" (هو).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
The mafʿūl bihi (direct object) was omitted, just as one says "Zayd struck" without mentioning the one struck, either because the hearer knows it or because you want to keep it vague for him. It has been said: the meaning is "by the night when it covers everything with its darkness", so that it becomes like a covering for it — and the day is not like that. On this is the saying of al-Dhubyānī: [al-Ṭawīl] 570-
فإنّك كاللّيل الّذي هو مدركي ... وإن خلت أنّ المنتأى عنك واسع
(For you are like the night, which will overtake me, even if I imagined that the place of refuge from you is wide.)

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى (10), he said: the Fire. If it is said: easing (taysīr) is only for good, so how has it come for hardship? The answer is that it is like فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ [Āl ʿImrān: 21], i.e., make what stands for them [Translator's note: the text reads «ما يا قوم لهم», evidently corrupt for «ما يقوم لهم»] in the place of good tidings. Sībawayh recited: [al-Wāfir] 571- تحيّة بينهم ضرب وجيع ("The greeting between them is a painful blow"). This is the view of the Basrans. And the view of al-Farrāʾ is that when good and evil come together and "giving good tidings" occurs for the good, it is permissible for the like of it to occur for the evil.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: ما is in the position of the accusative by يغني, i.e., "and what will his wealth ward off from him when he falls into the Fire?" Mujāhid held (that it means) "when he perishes", and this is said only of perishing. Radiya yardā [Translator's note: the text reads «ردى يردي»] and taraddā, when he falls; and radu'a the man yardu'u radāʾatan, and he is radīʾ, murdiʾ (bad).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: A lām of emphasis entered upon الهدى; the alif (of the article) was dropped so that it would not resemble the «لا» of negation, and because the lām is joined to what follows it.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: And likewise وَإِنَّ لَنا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولى (13).

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ ناراً تَلَظَّى (14): an imperfect verb, the original being تتلظّى. Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, that he read «تتلظّى»; and some of the memorisers (ḥuffāẓ) narrate from Ibn ʿUyayna with this chain the assimilation of the tāʾ into the tāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: The nunation must then be given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Mujāhid said: تلظّى means "blazes".

nahhas-irab:15-16.t: لا يَصْلاها إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى (15): there are two views on it. Abū ʿUbayda said: الْأَشْقَى is in the sense of al-shaqī (the wretched); and al-Farrāʾ said: al-ashqā is the one who is wretched in the knowledge of Allah, Glorified. The other view: "I have warned you of a blazing Fire which none will enter except the most wretched of the people of the Fire", and the most wretched of the people of the Fire are the disbelievers; and by this it indicates that others than the disbelievers enter the Fire because of their sins. Al-Farrāʾ said: الَّذِي كَذَّبَ, i.e., fell short; he took it from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so charged at so-and-so and did not hold back (fa-mā kadhaba)" [Translator's note: the text breaks off at «فما»].

nahhas-irab:17-18.t: I.e., he purifies himself of sins.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
I.e., he does not give charity in order to repay a person for a favour he had bestowed on him. On its meaning there is another view, which al-Farrāʾ mentioned: it refers to the future, i.e., he does not give charity in order to be repaid for his charity. Moreover, al-Farrāʾ made it a case of inversion (maqlūb), in the sense of "and he has no favour with anyone to be repaid", and recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 572-
وقد خفت حتّى ما تزيد مخافتي ... على وعل في ذي المطارة عاقل
(I have feared until my fear does not exceed that of a mountain goat taking refuge on Dhū al-Maṭāra.)
He interpreted it in the sense of "until the fear of a mountain goat does not exceed my fear". Abū Jaʿfar said: It is not permissible for the Book of Allah to be construed on inversion and far-fetched poetic necessities.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Genitive by conjunction (ʿaṭf); it is not a wāw of oath.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t:
إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلى (20) is accusative because it is an exception that is not of the kind of the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); the Basrans mentioned nothing other than this. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the implied form to be: "he does not spend except seeking the Face of his Lord"; and he permitted إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ in the nominative, because the meaning is "and no one has with him any favour to be repaid, except seeking the Face of his Lord". Abū Jaʿfar said: It was not read so, and it is also far-fetched, even though the grammarians have permitted it, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 573-
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلّا اليعافير وإلّا العيس
(And many a land in which there is no companion except the gazelles and the white camels.)
And some recited, from al-Nābigha: [al-Basīṭ] 574-
وقفت فيها أصيلا كي أسائلها ... عيّت جوابا وما بالرّبع من أحد
إلّا أواريّ لأيا ما أبيّنها ... والنّؤي كالحوض بالمظلومة الجلد
(I stood there in the late afternoon to question it; it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the encampment — except tethering-posts I could barely make out, and the trench like a cistern in the hard, untouched ground.)
The nominative in this is like وما لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزى (19) إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلى (20). And this is figurative (majāz), i.e., except seeking His good pleasure. وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضى (21), i.e., with the reward.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e., "and by His creating the male and the female". It has been said that «ما» is in the sense of الذي. Al-Farrāʾ permitted:
وما خلق الذكر والأنثى in the sense of "and by the One who created the male and the female". Abū Jaʿfar said: It is a far-fetched construal that «ما» be in the sense of «من»; moreover, we know of no one who read it so. But it has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: «والنّهار إذا تجلّى وما خلق الذكر والأنثى» [Translator's note: so in the text; the version usually reported in this ḥadīth is «والذَّكَرِ والأنثى»], and it is a conjunction.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى is) the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: سعيكم means your deeds.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the Basrans, and according to the Kufans (it is nominative) by the hāʾ (pronoun) referring back to it. Al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid said: "As for him who gives his zakāt and fears his Lord". Among the best things said about the meaning of وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى is what was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn Rāshid, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Ibn ʿUlayya, who said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind informed us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى, he said: "in the succession (al-khalaf)" [Translator's note: the text reads «بالحلف»; the report is known as «بالخَلَف», i.e., Allah's replacing what is spent]. This is a sound chain of transmission (isnād), and a meaning that fits the context of the speech.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: Juwaybir said, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: (لِلْيُسْرى means) for the Garden.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: On that view: he was miserly with his zakāt and considered himself free of need of the reward of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {وَمَا خَلَقَ}: «ما» may be in the sense of «مَنْ» (who), and this is the view of a group whose mention preceded in the previous sūra. It was also said: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «[i.e.] and by the Powerful One, of mighty power, Who was able to create the male and the female from a single fluid.» I say: the establishment of this view of his, what was objected against it and what was answered on its behalf have already been given in the previous sūra. Abū al-Dardāʾ read «والذَّكرِ والأنثى», and ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «والذي خَلَق»; and al-Kisāʾī — and Thaʿlab transmitted it from some of the early generations (salaf) — [read] «وما خَلَقَ الذَّكَرِ» with «الذكَرِ» in the genitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «As a badal (substitute) for the position of "ما خَلَقَ" in the sense of "وما خَلَقَه", i.e. and by what Allah created, the male; and implying "الله" was permissible because it is known that He alone creates.» The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «It may also be explained as [conjoined on] an imagined verbal noun, i.e. "and by the creation of the male", as in his saying:
4583 - تَطُوفُ العُفاةُ بأبوابِه ... كما طاف بالبَيْعَةِ الراهبِ
(Those seeking favours circle around his doors, as the monk circles around the church.)
with "الراهب" in the genitive on the supposition of the verbal noun having been pronounced, i.e. "like the circling of the monk".» End of quotation. What appears [to me] in explaining the verse [of poetry] is that its origin is «الراهبيّ» with the yāʾ of relation (nisba), relating to the attribute, then it was lightened; and this is rare, like their saying أَحْمري and دَوَّاري. This very explanation [applies] to the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4584 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَقِلْ في مَقيلٍ نَحْسُه مُتَغَيِّبِ
(…so take your midday rest in a resting-place whose ill omen is absent.)
which the Kufans cited as evidence for putting the fāʿil (agent) first. The majority read {تجلى} as a past verb, its fāʿil being a pronoun referring to the day. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr [read] «تتجلى» with two tāʾs, i.e. the sun. And «تُجْلي» was read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and sukūn on the jīm, i.e. also the sun; and there must be an omitted [pronoun] referring back to the day, i.e. "it [the sun] becomes manifest — or reveals [things] — in it".

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ}: This is the apodosis (jawāb) of the oath. It is also possible that it [the apodosis] is omitted, as was said regarding its parallels mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {أعطى}: He omitted the two objects of «أعطى», the object of «اتقى», and the object of «صَدَّقَ» [which would be] in the genitive with «على», because the purpose is the mention of these events without their attached elements (mutaʿallaqāt); likewise the attached elements of the stinginess and the self-sufficiency. And His saying: {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ للعسرى} is either by way of correspondence (muqābala) with His saying: {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لليسرى}, or because «نيسِّره» means "We prepare him", and preparing can be for ease and for hardship.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {وَمَا يُغْنِي}: «ما» may be negative, or a denying (inkārī) interrogative.
His saying: {تردى}: either from destruction, or from تردّى بأكفانِه (he wrapped himself in his shrouds), which is a metonymy for death, as in his saying:
4585 - وخُطَّا بأَطْرافِ الأسِنَّةِ مَضْجَعي ... ورُدَّا على عَيْنَيَّ فَضْلَ رِدائيا
(Mark out my resting-place with the tips of the spearheads, and draw the rest of my cloak back over my eyes.)
and the saying of another:
4586 - نَصيبُك مِمَّا تَجْمَعُ الدهرَ كلَّه ... رِداءان تلوى فيهما وحَنُوطُ
(Your share of all that you gather throughout time is two cloaks in which you are wrapped, and embalming spices.)

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {نَاراً تلظى}: It has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara that al-Bazzī doubles the tāʾ, and the doubling here is difficult because of the meeting of two sākin letters in it, not within the permitted limit; it is the counterpart of His saying {إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ} [al-Nūr: 15], which has already been given. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is read with kasra on the tanwīn and doubled tāʾ, and its explanation was mentioned at {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث} [al-Baqara: 267]." End of quotation. This is an odd reading, but it accords with analogy in that two sākin letters do not meet in it. As for his saying "its explanation was mentioned": what he said in al-Baqara is of no use at all here. For he said there: "It is read with a doubled tāʾ preceded by an alif, which is a combination of two sākin letters, and what made that permissible is the lengthening that is in the alif."

Ibn al-Zubayr, Sufyān, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Ṭalḥa read «تتلظى» with two tāʾs, which is the original form.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الأشقى}: It was said: «الأشقى» and «الأَتْقى» mean «الشقيّ» and «التقيّ» ("the wretched" and "the pious"), with no comparative sense in them, because the Fire is not restricted to the most wretched, and avoiding it is not restricted to the most pious. It was also said: rather they are in their normal sense, which is the view of al-Zamakhsharī. He said: "If you say: how did He say «لا يَصْلاها إلاَّ الأشقى» {وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الأتقى}, when it is known that every wretched person will burn in it and every pious person will be kept away from it, and that burning is not restricted to the most wretched of the wretched, nor salvation to the most pious of the pious? And if you claim that He made «النار» indefinite so as to mean a particular Fire restricted to the most wretched, what will you do with His saying {وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الأتقى}? For it is known that even the most iniquitous of the Muslims is kept away from that particular Fire, not only the most pious of them. I say: the verse comes in the weighing of the two states of a great one among the polytheists and a great one among the believers. So it was intended to be emphatic in describing their two opposite qualities. So it said «الأشقى» and made it restricted to the burning, as though the Fire had been created only for him; and it said «الأتقى» and made it restricted to the salvation, as though Paradise had been created only for him. It was also said: they are Abū Jahl or Umayya b. Khalaf, and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him." End of quotation. So his answer comes down to the two being specific individuals.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {يتزكى}: The majority read {يتزكى}, the imperfect of «تَزَكَّى». Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, the Commander of the Faithful, read «يزكى», assimilating the tāʾ into the zāy. There are two views on this clause. One: that it is in the position of ḥāl from the agent of «يُؤْتي», i.e. "he gives it, purifying himself by it." The second: that it has no grammatical position, on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) for the ṣila of «الذي». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned both, and the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] judged it to be forced.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {تجزى}: It is an adjective of «نعمة», i.e. "that is repaid to the human being." It was brought as a passive imperfect only for the sake of the verse-endings, since the original would be «يُجْزيها إياه» or «يُجْزِيه إياها».

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ ابتغآء}: There are two views on its accusative. One: that it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be a mafʿūl lahu in meaning, because the meaning is: he gives his wealth only seeking the face of his Lord, not to repay a favour." He took this from the saying of al-Farrāʾ, who said: "It is put in the accusative on the interpretation: «ما أعْطَيْتُك ابتغاءَ جزائِك، بل ابتغاءَ وجهِ اللَّهِ تعالى» ('I did not give to you seeking your recompense, but seeking the face of Allah the Exalted')." The second: that it is accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), since it does not fall under the genus of «مِنْ نعمة». This is the reading of the majority, I mean the accusative with the lengthened alif.

Yaḥyā read it in the nominative, lengthened, as a badal (substitute) for the position of «مِنْ نعمة», because the position of that is nominative: either as agent or as mubtadaʾ, and «مِنْ» is redundant (mazīda) in both cases. The badal is the dialect of Tamīm, because they treat a discontinuous exception in a non-affirmative context like a continuous one. Al-Zamakhsharī cited for both the accusative and the badal the saying of Bishr b. Abī Khāzim:

[Translator's note: the verse numbers are garbled in the source, printed as «458 - 7-» and «458 - 8-»; from the sequence they should be 4587 and 4588.]

4587 - أَضْحَتْ خَلاءً قِفاراً أَنيسَ بها ... إلاَّ الجآذِرُ والظِّلْمانَُِ تَخْتَلِفُ
(It has become empty and desolate, with no companion in it except the gazelle fawns and the ostriches, which come and go)

and the saying of another, for the nominative:

4588 - وبَلْدَةٍ ليس بها أنيسُ ... إلاَّ اليَعافيرُ وإلاَّ العِيْسُ
(And a land with no companion in it, except the gazelles and the pale camels)

Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative in «ابتغاء» as a badal for the position of «نِعْمَةٍ», but that is remote." I say: it is as though he had not come across it as a reading; his calling it remote is itself remote, since it is a widespread dialect. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ابْتِغا» shortened.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {وَلَسَوْفَ يرضى}: This is the answer to an implied oath. The majority read «يرضى» as active. It was also read as passive, from «أَرْضاه الله», which is close to His saying at the end of Sūrat Ṭā Hā {لَعَلَّكَ ترضى} and {ترضى} [Ṭā Hā: 130].

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (وَمَا خَلَقَ): «مَا» is in the sense of «مَنْ» (who), or it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). On the first view, «مَنْ» is an allusion to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and (الذَّكَرَ) is the mafʿūl (object); or it may refer to the created being, in which case «الذَّكَرَ» is a badal (substitute) for «مَنْ», and the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى (١١)).
(وَمَا يُغْنِي): it may be a negation, and it may be an interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّى (١٤)).
(نَارًا تَلَظَّى) is read with a kasra on the tanwīn (nunation) and a doubled tāʾ; its justification has been mentioned at the words of the Exalted: (وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا الْخَبِيثَ).

ukberi-tibyan:19-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزَى (١٩) إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَى (٢٠)).
The words of the Exalted (إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ): this is an exception from outside the genus (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and the implied form is: «لَكِنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ» (but he did that seeking the face of his Lord).

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Layl
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا يَغْشى﴾ ﴿والنَّهارِ إذا تَجَلّى﴾: this is an oath, whose answer is ﴿إنَّ سَعْيَكم لَشَتّى﴾ [al-Layl: 4] ("your striving is surely diverse"), that is: the striving of the believer and the unbeliever is surely different; between them is a great distance. The meaning of "when the night covers the earth" is: the horizon and everything between the sky and the earth is hidden; and "the day when it shines forth" is: when it becomes clear and manifest.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَما خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ والأُنْثى﴾ ("and by what created the male and the female"): as we explained it in His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ وما بَناها﴾ [al-Shams: 5].

zajjaj:5-6.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأمّا مَن أعْطى واتَّقى﴾ ﴿وَصَدَّقَ بِالحُسْنى﴾ ("as for him who gives and is mindful, and affirms the best"): in the exegesis it is that it was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah have mercy on him. He had bought a group whom the polytheists were torturing to make them apostatise from Islam, among them Bilāl. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, described him as having given in mindfulness (taqwā) and affirmed the best, because he will be recompensed for it. And it was said: "he affirmed" because He replaces it for him, by His saying: ﴿وَما أنْفَقْتُمْ مِن شَيْءٍ فَهو يُخْلِفُهُ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 39] ("and whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it").

zajjaj:7-7.t: And He said: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرى﴾ ("We shall ease him toward ease"): that is, toward the easy matter which none is able to do except the believers.

zajjaj:8-9.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأمّا مَن بَخِلَ واسْتَغْنى﴾ ﴿وَكَذَّبَ بِالحُسْنى﴾ ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى﴾ [al-Layl: 10] ("but as for him who is miserly and deems himself self-sufficient, and denies the best, We shall ease him toward hardship"): it was revealed about a man whom I dislike to mention; and it is comprehensive of everyone who is miserly and denies, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, recompenses him, or brings ruin upon [his wealth].

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى﴾: [toward] the punishment and the difficult matter.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَما يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مالُهُ إذا تَرَدّى﴾ ("and his wealth will not avail him when he falls"): it was said: when he dies; and it was said: when he falls headlong into the Fire.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿إنَّ عَلَيْنا لَلْهُدى﴾ ("upon Us is the guidance"): that is, it is upon Us to make clear the way of guidance from the way of misguidance.

zajjaj:14-16.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ ﴿لا يَصْلاها إلا الأشْقى﴾ ﴿الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ("so I have warned you of a Fire that blazes, which none will enter but the most wretched, who denied and turned away"): ”تَلَظّى“ means "it flares up and burns". This verse is the one on account of which the people of irjāʾ (the Murjiʾa, who defer judgement on sinners) held their doctrine of irjāʾ: they claimed that none enters the Fire except an unbeliever, because of His saying ﴿لا يَصْلاها إلا الأشْقى﴾ ﴿الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وتَوَلّى﴾. But it is not as they supposed: this is a particular Fire, described specifically; none enters this Fire except the most wretched who denied and turned away. The people of the Fire have different stations; among them is His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُنافِقِينَ في الدَّرْكِ الأسْفَلِ مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 145] ("the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire"). And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: whatever He has threatened with any kind of punishment, it is possible that He punish with it. And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ ويَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشاءُ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 48] ("Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills"). If everyone who did not associate partners with Allah were not punished, there would be no benefit in His saying ”وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذَلِكَ“ ("and He forgives what is less than that"), and He would [simply] forgive what is less than that.

zajjaj:17-18.t: And His saying: ﴿وَسَيُجَنَّبُها الأتْقى﴾ ﴿الَّذِي يُؤْتِي مالَهُ يَتَزَكّى﴾ ("but the most mindful will be kept away from it, who gives his wealth to purify himself"): that is, he seeks to be pure in Allah's sight, not seeking thereby to be seen or heard of. It was revealed about Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿وَما لأحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِن نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزى﴾ ("and no one has with him any favour to be repaid"): that is, he did not do that in repayment of a kindness rendered to him.
﴿إلا ابْتِغاءَ وجْهِ رَبِّهِ الأعْلى﴾ [al-Layl: 20] ("only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High"): that is, only seeking His reward.

zajjaj:21-21.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضى﴾ ("and he will surely be pleased"): that is, he will enter Paradise, as He said: ﴿ارْجِعِي إلى رَبِّكِ راضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً﴾ [al-Fajr: 28] ﴿فادْخُلِي في عِبادِي﴾ [al-Fajr: 29] ﴿وادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي﴾ [al-Fajr: 30].
